title: Smart Salary NSW Health: Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay with a 38-Hour Week
description: Use the smart salary nsw health approach to convert hourly rates to annual, fortnightly, and monthly pay. Includes tax, super, and award rates from Fair Work.
salarySummary: For a 38-hour week, annual gross pay is hourly rate × 38 × 52, with super paid on top and tax deducted using 2026–27 rates.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary using a 38-hour week?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by 38 hours per week, then by 52 weeks per year. For example, $30/hour × 38 × 52 = $59,280 gross annual pay. The fortnightly amount is weekly pay × 2. This assumes no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

faqs.q: Does the calculator include casual loading?
faqs.a: Yes, but only if you tick the '25% casual loading' checkbox. The base hourly rate you enter should not already include casual loading. The calculator adds 25% on top to match the casual minimum rate of $33.05/hour (from $26.44/hour) as set by the Fair Work Ombudsman.

faqs.q: How is superannuation treated in the annual estimate?
faqs.a: Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid on top of your gross pay. It is not deducted from your take-home pay. The estimate stops at the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Salary packaging, such as through the smart salary nsw health calculator, can further affect your net pay.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Pay: Hourly to Annual Conversion

When you have an hourly rate or a salary offer, knowing your annual, fortnightly, and monthly equivalents helps you compare jobs and budget. This guide uses a standard 38-hour week and a 52-week year, as assumed by the Fair Work Ombudsman for full-time employees. The formula is simple: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 = annual gross pay**. For a fortnight, multiply the weekly amount by 2.

### The 38-Hour Week and the National Minimum Wage

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for a 38-hour week. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the minimum casual rate $33.05 per hour. This loading compensates for not receiving paid leave. Always check which award applies to your job, as award rates may be higher than the minimum. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides [pay guides](/blog) for each award, including the Health Professionals and Support Services Award and the Social, Community, Home Care and Disability Services Industry Award.

### Casual Loading: What You Need to Know

If you are a casual employee, your base hourly rate should be entered without the 25% loading. The calculator has a checkbox to add the loading on top. For example, if your award rate is $26.44, ticking the box gives $33.05. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading, as that would double the loading.

### Tax and Medicare for 2026–27

Your annual gross pay is subject to income tax and the Medicare levy. The 2026–27 resident tax rates are:
- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15%
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30%
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37%
- Over $190,000: 45%

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. The calculator uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed. This is an estimate only; your actual tax may differ due to offsets, the Medicare levy surcharge, or HELP repayments.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Employers must pay super guarantee of 12% of your ordinary earnings, on top of your gross pay. This is not deducted from your take-home pay. The maximum contribution base for 2026–27 is $270,830. For example, if your annual gross is $80,000, your employer contributes an extra $9,600 to your super fund. You can learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) on our site.

### Salary Packaging and the Smart Salary NSW Health Calculator

For employees in New South Wales Health, salary packaging can reduce your taxable income. The **smart salary nsw health** calculator from Smartsalary Pty Ltd provides an estimate of potential savings, based on the 2026–27 tax rates and the May 2026 Federal Budget. It accounts for items like meal entertainment, novated leases, and superannuation contributions. However, it does not include individual eligibility for cost-of-living measures or your employer’s accounting methods. Always seek professional advice before making salary packaging decisions.

### Award Rates vs. Minimum Wage

The National Minimum Wage is the floor, but many industries have award rates that are higher. For example, the Health Professionals and Support Services Award sets specific classifications and pay points. The Fair Work Ombudsman’s [pay guides](/blog) list minimum rates for full-time, part-time, and casual employees, including allowances and penalty rates. If your employer has an enterprise agreement, that agreement may override the award. Use the [reference tables](/data) on our site to compare rates.

### Putting It All Together: A Worked Example

Suppose you are a full-time health professional earning $35 per hour under the Health Professionals Award. Your annual gross is $35 × 38 × 52 = $69,160. Fortnightly pay is $35 × 38 × 2 = $2,660. After tax (using 2026–27 rates) and 2% Medicare, your estimated take-home pay is about $54,000 per year (exact amount depends on your circumstances). Your employer also pays 12% super ($8,299) on top. If you are casual, your rate would be $35 × 1.25 = $43.75 per hour, giving annual gross of $86,450.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
